subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Viscosity: The Thickness of Fluids
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Viscosity: The Thickness of Fluids.

hook.text: Honey crawls off a spoon. Water splashes. The difference is viscosity.

buildup.text: Viscosity measures how strongly a fluid resists flowing and shearing.

discovery.text: High viscosity means more drag. Pumping honey takes far more energy.

twist.text: Heating oil makes it thin. Cold makes it thick. Temperature rules viscosity.

climax.text: Pipeline engineers heat crude oil in winter so it flows through pipes.

punchline.text: Thickness decides how hard a fluid fights the pump.

quiz.question: Why do pipeline operators heat crude oil in winter?
options: To prevent ice from forming inside the pipe
Cold oil gets thicker and harder to pump, so heating restores flow
Heated oil expands and pushes itself through the pipe
